newsitem.title: USA: New Mexico regulators approve utilities' merger.
newsitem.headline: New Mexico regulators approve utilities' merger.

text.p: The New Mexico Public Utility Commission late Tuesday approved the merger of Southwestern Public Service Co and Public Service Co of Colorado to create New Century Energies, Southwestern Public Service said.

The commission found the merger to be in the public interest and approved SPS's plans for a $1.2 million annual credit to its New Mexico retail customers to pass along savings resulting from the merger, the utility said.
It said state approvals have now been received in New Mexico, Colorado, Kansas and Wyoming.
In Oklahoma, regulators have approved passing along savings to customers and said they will not oppose the merger. Texas regulators are to consider the merger February 5.
An administrative law judge has recommended approval by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.
Pending those approvals, approval by the Securities and Exchange Commission and other conditions, the merger is targeted for completion this spring, Southwestern PS said.
